frequency_question: How often do newly established structural liquidity or buyback programs successfully scale up to their target operational volumes rather than remaining capped, scaling back, or stalling due to structural market frictions?
membership_rule: Includes major new Treasury/Fed intervention programs (e.g., post-2008 large-scale asset purchase programs, Supplementary Financing Program, major Treasury buyback initiatives). Excludes routine daily repo operations or standard monetary policy rate adjustments.

cases.name: Federal Reserve Maturity Extension Program (Operation Twist)
Fed Quantitative Tightening (Balance Sheet Roll-off Caps)
U.S. Treasury Regular Debt Buyback Program (2024 launch)

coverage_note: 6 named major modern interventions; representative of structural program scaling under assumed institutional will.
known_gaps: Excludes minor tactical adjustments that were not structural programs.
skeleton: 6 historical major structural intervention programs or scaling phases evaluated for reaching full targeted operational deployment.
validity_reason: Institutional mechanics of Treasury and Federal Reserve market interventions remain stable across decades barring major legislative overhauls.
